result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md in full (S1-S14), docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md in full, and every changed file myself (apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaff.ts+test, domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts+test, domain/user.ts's getUserByTgUsername, handlers/staff.ts, handlers/checkin.ts, i18n additions, index.ts wiring) -- did not trust REVIEWER's or BACKEND-DEV's reports. git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-018 confirms no schema/migration file (db/schema.ts untouched, no .sql) so the S13 migration sign-off duty is not triggered. S2 (primary focus) PASS, independently re-derived: read checkEventStaffAuthorization's 4 branches myself (user===null -> no-user; staffRow===null -> not-staff-for-event; isFinished(endsAt,evaluationTime) -> event-ended; else ok) -- none reference `.role` or any Talk/speaker field. Confirmed by git grep that requireEventStaffForEvent/checkEventStaffAuthorization has exactly one call site in non-test code (handlers/checkin.ts) -- no alternate handler grants check-in-equivalent access, so the expiry/existence check cannot be bypassed by any other path. Confirmed the /checkin stub is genuinely inert beyond authorize-and-acknowledge: no qr_token parsing, no registrations read/write, no checked_in_at reference anywhere in the diff (grepped). Confirmed AC2's structural reasoning (design section 0.4): addEventStaff/removeEventStaff write only to event_staff, never to users.role, so the pre-existing checkOrganizerForChapter refusal on /venue_new and /event_publish is unaffected -- verified by reading both mutation functions, neither touches the users table. AC6 own re-derivation: git grep -in speaker -- apps/bot/src returns no matches (exit 1). S1: N/A with reason -- addEventStaff/removeEventStaff target an existing User row (found via getUserByTgUsername) and write only to event_staff (event_id, user_id), no PII field; the design's own defensive check (targetUser.tgId === null -> staff.userNotFound) additionally refuses to staff a User row that was pre-created without ever completing /start, so no walk-in-style storage-before-consent path exists here. S8 PASS: read addEventStaff and removeEventStaff -- each is a single db.transaction containing exactly one row mutation and exactly one writeAuditLog call, mirroring venue.ts's createVenue/deleteVenue shape byte for byte; no bulk/admin bypass path exists since these are the only two mutators of event_staff. Username-enumeration question (explicitly checked): getUserByTgUsername is called from handlers/staff.ts AFTER requireOrganizerForChapter's authorization check in both /staff_add and /staff_remove (read the handler bodies top to bottom to confirm ordering) -- an unauthorized caller (non-organizer, or organizer of the wrong chapter) is refused with staff.notAuthorized before the username lookup ever runs, so no username-existence oracle is exposed to an unauthorized actor. An already-authorized organizer/owner CAN distinguish staff.userNotFound (username has no User row) from alreadyAssigned/success (it does) for ANY tg_username regardless of chapter, since getUserByTgUsername has no chapter scoping -- this discloses only bare username-existence (a boolean already partially guessed by the caller who typed it), never phone/email/employer/PII, to an actor already trusted with organizer-level authority over other people's registrations; not a violation of any stated S1-S14 item, noted as an observation, not a blocker. PII/new-exposure check: assignment/removal AuditLog payloads carry only eventId/targetUserId(internal uuid)/eventTitle -- no phone/email/tg_username in payload (S11 PASS). Notification bodies (assignmentNotificationBody/removalNotificationBody) are sent only to the target's own chat id and name only the event title -- no other staff member's or event's data is disclosed (no new S3-adjacent leak). checkin.ts's not-found-before-authorization ordering matches pre-existing venue/event edit/delete precedent (event ids are not secret), not a new disclosure. S3/S4/S6/S7/S9/S10/S12/S14: N/A, none of qr_token/InviteCode/checked_in_at/capacity/notification-job/marketing-send/export/Profile-publish code is touched by this diff (grepped for each). S5 FAIL, decisive: security-invariants.md S5's negative case states plainly 'the non-staff refusal that returns an error but writes no audit row -- the one case where the log matters most is an attempted unauthorized scan.' This diff's handlers/checkin.ts IS a live, reachable check-in-surface gate today (that is this requirement's own stated purpose per its title, 'the staff-only check-in surface gate') -- any Telegram user can invoke /checkin <event_id> right now, and every refusal path (no-user, not-staff-for-event, event-ended) returns a reply with zero AuditLog write, confirmed by reading handlers/checkin.ts end to end and by grepping for writeAuditLog/AuditLog in checkin.ts and eventStaffAuthorization.ts (no matches in either). The design (section 0.3/6.1) argues this is deferred to REQ-028/029 on the theory that S5's table describes the full qr_token scanning flow, which does not exist yet -- but the specific sub-property at risk (an attempted-unauthorized-scan is left unlogged) does not depend on qr_token existing: the authorization gate itself is what is being probed by an unauthorized actor, and that gate is real and live in this diff. Confirmed this is not schema-blocked: audit_log.actor_user_id is nullable (db/schema.ts line 314, 'a genuinely system-initiated action ... has no human actor') and entity_id is a plain non-FK uuid (line 321), so a refusal row (entity: 'event' or 'event_staff', entityId: event.id, actorUserId: resolved user.id when available else null, payload noting the refusal reason and no PII) is writable today with the schema exactly as it stands -- there is no technical blocker forcing the deferral, only a scoping choice, and per core-directives.md's re-derive rule this scoping choice does not survive re-derivation against the invariant's own stated worst case. This is the sole blocking finding; every other applicable item (S1, S2, S8, S11, plus the enumeration question) passes as detailed above.

issues.description: S5 violation: apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts's authorization refusal path (no-user / not-staff-for-event / event-ended, all three reasons from domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts's CheckInAuthorizationResult) writes no AuditLog row. security-invariants.md S5 requires 'Scanner is not staff -> Refuse and write an AuditLog row', and states explicitly that this is the one case where the log matters most. /checkin is a live, reachable command in this diff (not a not-yet-built future surface), so an attempted unauthorized check-in access attempt is currently unlogged. audit_log.actor_user_id is nullable and entity_id is a non-FK uuid (db/schema.ts), so no schema change is required to fix this -- add a writeAuditLog call (e.g. action 'checkin.unauthorized_attempt' or similar, entity 'event', entityId: event.id, actorUserId: the resolved user's id when resolveActingUser found one else null, payload with no PII) on the refusal branch in handlers/checkin.ts, or in requireEventStaffForEvent itself so every caller of the gate gets it uniformly. Route back to BACKEND-DEV/CODE-DESIGNER to decide the exact call site and payload shape, then re-run this gate.
